project.name: codex
project.identity: The OpenAI Codex CLI: a local coding agent that inspects repositories, edits files, and runs development checks through a terminal-oriented workflow.
project.audience: Developers and maintainers using a local coding-agent CLI with explicit repository and execution boundaries.
project.core_loop: Invoke the agent, inspect repository context, make a bounded change, run checks, and review the resulting evidence.
project.north_star: A developer can use the local CLI to make attributable repository changes with clear verification and ownership boundaries.
not_this: The Codex Web or ChatGPT product surface
A claim that this checkout is a released provider artifact
Proof of provider-native execution from source inspection alone

mvp.definition: The CLI can be built or run locally with documented repository-facing behavior and a reviewable change loop.

complete_product.definition: The CLI provides a stable local coding-agent workflow with tested command behavior, distribution evidence, and clear provider/runtime boundaries.

outcomes.name: The local CLI supports an inspect, edit, and test loop that is understandable to repository users.

layers.intended: Codex is intended to help developers work through local repository changes.
layers.planned: Repository guidance and the Rust CLI layout describe the local coding-agent surface.
layers.implemented: README.md, AGENTS.md, and codex-rs/README.md document the CLI and its repository context.
layers.verified: This contract is grounded in source and documentation; a fresh end-user CLI smoke is not recorded here.

evidence.note: CLI purpose and user-facing entry point.

blockers.summary: A fresh forward-facing CLI smoke and distribution readback are not recorded in this bootstrap contract.

outcomes.name: Local source, branch state, and provider ownership are kept distinct from released or provider-native claims.

layers.intended: The project should make local, released, and provider-native states distinguishable.
layers.planned: Repository instructions and branch policy preserve release/default lines separately from development work.
layers.implemented: The fork checkout provides source and documentation; active local worktrees remain distinct from the canonical development target and neither is a release receipt.
layers.verified: The user-owned fork jakyeamos/codex is the canonical provider target and exposes live main and dev branches; upstream openai/codex remains a separate source repository.

drift.summary: The repository documents a local CLI, but current end-user behavior and release distribution are not proven by this contract.
